# DS-000011 and DS-000018: deep knowledge corpus audit

Audit timestamp: 2026-09-24 11:32 UTC (16:32 Asia/Karachi). Branch: `chore/full-local-data-sync-and-senior-health-acquisition`. Starting HEAD: `c740f89212dd7a1c59c273fce07e2613f24a68c4`. Starting worktree: one unrelated untracked `.codex/environments/` directory; no tracked changes. This audit changed no source, catalog, registry, or production code. Evidence labels used below: **VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY** (directly inspected bytes or rows), **VERIFIED_FROM_PRIMARY_WEB_SOURCE** (linked current platform documentation), **DERIVED** (repeatable calculation), **INFERRED** (reasoned interpretation), **UNVERIFIED**, **CONFLICTING**, **STALE**. A label on a source claim does not certify its causal explanation.

## 1. Executive Summary

**DS-000011 is a mixed creative and creator education library, not an official YouTube training set.** Seventeen physical documents contain sixteen textually unique works: hook and script templates, title/thumbnail/SEO checklists, AI image/video prompting, a senior-health creator operating prompt, and two long, mixed-source algorithm compilations. Almost all original authors, publication dates, and original URLs are missing. One hook PDF is repeated under a second filename. Its strongest use is as a *dated, source-labeled creative checklist and hypothesis library*, not platform truth. [VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY: `data/manifests/DS-000011.md`; `document_records`; J files below.]

**DS-000018 is one user-supplied Google Doc snapshot with 63 tabs, not 63 official updates.** Tabs hold third-party video titles, descriptions/chapters, and transcripts or scripts (245,914 manifest words); two pairs reproduce substantially the same videos, leaving **61 unique substantive video-source texts**. Stored source dates and authors are poorly captured. Its 33-row claim artifact selects passages from only seven tabs, and the later validation artifact disposes all 33 claims: 10 supported, 12 partially supported, 1 contradicted, 8 lacking primary support, 2 not currently verifiable. These are *disposition counts*, not 33 proven algorithm changes. [VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY: `data/manifests/DS-000018.md`; E archive and `source-manifest.json`; `data/intelligence/global/youtube-algorithm-primary-validation-2026-09-04.md` final synthesis.]

No original first-party YouTube Analytics exports, private viewer data, ranking weights, or platform experiment datasets live in either corpus. Two DS-000018 tabs preserve platform-attributed interview speech, but the archived transcript alone does not independently establish speaker identity or verbatim accuracy. Current official guidance supports personalized, surface-specific discovery, appeal/engagement/satisfaction, contextual Search relevance, and cross-format discovery; it does not support universal CTR/retention thresholds, a compulsory separate Shorts channel, a deterministic 48-hour gate, or a secret trust score. [VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY: J, E; VERIFIED_FROM_PRIMARY_WEB_SOURCE: section 17.]

The DS-000018 source Doc is [the user-supplied multi-tab document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14F1A38ngCbsn2ABWD-gRmUaLL_8utow31VLGHFEANJU/edit?usp=sharing); the raw ZIP is a snapshot, not Google's native original bytes. [VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY: E manifest.]

Each physical source is an immutable `RAW_SOURCE`; catalog `source_files`, `document_records`, manifests and derived intelligence point back to it. The DS-000011 registry compresses selected works into 17 rules; the DS-000018 registry repeats the 33 separately validated claims. These layers do not make the original source authoritative. `scripts/run_youtube_intelligence.py` and `scripts/report_channel_strategy_intelligence.py` produce channel-relative plans/diagnoses; the latter contains the global training registry. No production RAG or vector DB exists. [VERIFIED_FROM_REPOSITORY: `docs/Database.md`, `data/catalog/README.md`, both manifests, strategy script.]

Ten IDs already exist in the CH-000004 catalog. On 2026-10-09, the public

# What If forensic integration workflow

## Current contract and evidence boundaries

Release 1.0.0 supplies 14 media sources and 11,585 source-declared observations. The reviewed crosswalk has 12 verified mappings and two unresolved mappings. Ten verified mappings exist in the canonical CH-000004 inventory. X97DDWvxaqQ and 9VG0yqq_PHM remain unregistered with acquired transcript evidence pending; ownership is independently verified. PR #17 is canonical; use the reviewed metadata packet and normal supplied-workbook importer with exact `--transcript-pending-id` declarations (see [registration contract](TRANSCRIPT_PENDING_REGISTRATION.md)). Unknown metrics and content format remain NULL, and no fabricated transcript row is permitted. The selected canonical inventory has 83 unique What If videos; this integration has created zero videos and modified zero historical snapshots or transcripts.

The external corpus is immutable. Configure its location at runtime; no code assumes a home directory or machine name:

```bash
export YIOS_WHAT_IF_CORPUS_ROOT="/path/to/video data of what if"
python scripts/validate_what_if_source_contract.py
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py
```

Run commands from repository root in a Python 3.12 environment with declared dependencies installed. First creation reports CREATED; the second run reports UNCHANGED. Promotion reports UNCHANGED when reproducing the already committed index.

## Data flow and durable local staging

The adapter validates the release manifest, source index, crosswalk and actual media hashes, then reads only eight canonical MASTER CSVs. It does not import legacy output or copy media. Normalization joins by exact approved YouTube identity, never by title. Unresolved and unregistered identities are held, not rejected or silently promoted.

Generated local staging lives at `data/staging/what-if-forensic/v1.0.0/` relative to repository root and is ignored by Git. Keep this directory in the durable checkout rather than a disposable worktree. It contains eight JSONL tables and deterministic `manifest.json`, which records release, transformation, source-manifest hash, catalog identity hash, accepted/held/rejected counts, table sizes and checksums. `lifecycle.json` separately records its UTC creation timestamp and deterministic manifest checksum. Keeping wall-clock metadata separate preserves byte-identical evidence reproduction. Existing creation time survives repeated generation. Old valid stages acquire lifecycle metadata only after their deterministic files validate.

Every normalized observation preserves canonical video ID, source video ID, slug, release, table, local row ID, CSV row number, timing, supplied confidence, media hash, original fields and transformation version. A source reference resolves as configured corpus root plus `production_intelligence_brain/01_master_data/<table>.csv#row=<n>`; the fragment identifies the CSV row and is not part of the filesystem path.

Current accepted/held/rejected rows:

| Table | Source | Accepted and promoted | Held | Rejected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MASTER_WORDS | 7,864 | 5,817 | 2,047 | 0 |
| MASTER_SENTENCES | 604 | 485 | 119 | 0 |
| MASTER_SHOTS | 200 | 146 | 54 | 0 |
| MASTER_STATES | 581 | 352 | 229 | 0 |
| MASTER_MOTIONS | 438 | 289 | 149 | 0 |
| MASTER_ASSETS | 448 | 323 | 125 | 0 |
| MASTER_AUDIO_EVENTS | 29 | 21 | 8 | 0 |
| MASTER_AUDIO_VISUAL_SYNC | 1,421 | 894 | 527 | 0 |
| Total | 11,585 | 8,327 | 3,258 | 0 |

## Promotion and Editing/Visual consumption

Promotion reads the durable stage, revalidates every table checksum, counts, identity digest, observation key and provenance, then produces `data/intelligence/channels/CH-000004/forensic-observation-index-v1.json`. A different existing index fails with PROMOTION_CONFLICT; it is never replaced automatically. Promotion does not write to SQLite.

```bash
python scripts/query_what_if_forensics.py --video-id mEUqVgGf4e0 > /tmp/what-if-query.json
python scripts/run_youtube_intelligence.py \
  --channel CH-000004 --opportunity CH-000004-OP-001 \
  --generated-on 2026-10-09 --output-dir /tmp/what-if-production-plan
```

The compact query validates stage/index agreement before returning sampled shot pacing, state progression, motion actions/relationships, asset types and recurrence across unique videos, audio timing, narration/visual offsets, and the first 30 seconds of narration/edit pacing. Missing or non-finite timing never becomes a numeric measurement. Sampled shots do not establish complete-video coverage; changes per minute use sampled durations only. Recommendations remain EVIDENCE_BACKED_HYPOTHESIS, retain exact source rows and supplied confidence, and make no causal performance claim.

The orchestrator resolves opportunity video IDs through the canonical catalog and attaches matching guidance to the Editing/Visual blueprint. It preserves Topic, Packaging, Hook and Script artifacts. Four matching canonical videos contribute 2,381 observations and 24 cited hypotheses to the dated OP-001 example, without adding any channel samples. If local staging is absent, forensic consumption is explicitly NOT_AVAILABLE; if staging or index is changed, consumption fails closed. Historical editing reports remain preserved rather than rewritten.

## Review an update before promotion

Do not edit generated staging. Regenerate a candidate directory and candidate index, inspect the delta, and preserve current stage/index until review succeeds:

```bash
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py --output /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py \
  --stage /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate --output /tmp/what-if-index-candidate.json
python -m json.tool data/staging/what-if-forensic/v1.0.0/manifest.json > /tmp/what-if-before.json
python -m json.tool /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate/manifest.json > /tmp/what-if-after.json
diff -u /tmp/what-if-before.json /tmp/what-if-after.json
git diff --no-index -- \
  data/intelligence/channels/CH-000004/forensic-observation-index-v1.json \
  /tmp/what-if-index-candidate.json
```

`diff` exits 1 for a legitimate difference. Review counts, mappings, media hashes, release and transformation changes. For a new source release, preserve the old corpus and contract; use a new versioned source contract and stage path with `--contract` and `--output`. After approval, archive the previous ignored stage outside the active path and replace it with the validated candidate. Update the reviewed index in an atomic PR and regenerate dated production outputs. Never change a recorded hash merely to suppress a mismatch.

A source table or identity change invalidates staging/promotion; regeneration is required. Source-declared evidence and AI recommendations stay separate. No forensic row is an independent channel sample.

## Identity refresh and unresolved sources

The owner explicitly authorized a narrow official YouTube Data API refresh for CH-000004 on 2026-10-09, superseding the no-API rule only for this task. Repository currently has controlled Apify acquisition, but no existing `channels.list`/uploads/`playlistItems.list` acquisition implementation; no YouTube/Google API credential was available in the execution environment. Apify acquisition requires a separate approved cost cap and was not run as a substitute.

The two exact held IDs already have independent official identity evidence (2026-10-10); this full-list refresh limitation is not an ownership-verification blocker. There is currently no executable official refresh command to document honestly. Do not invoke a guessed script or register videos from search snippets. Once API authorization is available, the official acquisition must follow: `channels.list(part=contentDetails)` to identify the channel's uploads playlist; paginate `playlistItems.list(part=contentDetails)`; then `videos.list(part=snippet)` for exact channel ownership, title and publish time. Preserve sanitized response provenance and retrieval timestamp; register only genuine new IDs through the catalog registration workflow with append-only metadata snapshots. Review a 83-video baseline diff before publication. Credential values must remain environment-only.

SRC01 candidate U8F7UNK9jco has a matching sunset question on the official public video search result. SRC02 candidate qu8nx1qUwEU has matching visible-light question text. Their media metadata contains encoding/duration information but no authoritative video ID. Direct official page fetches were throttled. These are research candidates, not verified source-byte identity joins; crosswalk stays UNRESOLVED and promotion excludes both.

## Rollback

Catalog identities, snapshots and transcripts are not changed by stage/promotion/query work, so no data migration rollback is needed. Preserve the immutable external corpus and ignored stage.

For a published change, revert the specific integration merge in a new review branch, selecting the exact merge SHA from GitHub. Do not reset shared main or force-push:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git switch -c codex/what-if-rollback origin/main
git revert -m 1 <integration-merge-sha>
python -m pytest -q
git diff --check
```

Review dependent later commits before reverting; revert dependent units newest first. Submit the revert through normal PR/CI/exact-head merge. For local generated staging rollback, move the current ignored stage to a retained archive path and regenerate the previous reviewed contract at its deterministic path. Restore the matching reviewed promotion index via a PR. No raw media or historical evidence should be deleted.

## Privacy and raw-media policy

No raw MP4, audio, dense frames, Studio exports, credentials, temporary query outputs, or duplicated release packages may enter this What If integration. Keep source corpus and generated stages local. Commit only reviewed contracts, checksums, code/tests/docs and derived summaries with provenance. New private-derived analytics belong under ignored first-party storage.

Pre-existing tracked audio/frames/private-derived artifacts are separately classified in [repository safety review](audits/WHAT_IF_REPOSITORY_SAFETY_2026-10-09.md). They are not silently removed by this integration. Broader repository sharing or history rewriting requires an explicit owner/security decision.

## Documentation entry points

- [Staging and promotion](FORENSIC_STAGING_AND_PROMOTION.md)
- [Provenance lifecycle](PROVENANCE.md)
- [Data privacy](DATA_PRIVACY.md)
- [Update workflow](UPDATE_WORKFLOW.md)
- [Rollback](ROLLBACK.md)

Commands remain centralized above to prevent conflicting copies.

## Current contract and evidence boundaries

Release 1.0.0 supplies 14 media sources and 11,585 source-declared observations. The reviewed crosswalk has 12 verified mappings and two unresolved mappings. Ten verified mappings exist in the canonical CH-000004 inventory. X97DDWvxaqQ and 9VG0yqq_PHM remain unregistered pending official acquisition. The selected canonical inventory has 83 unique What If videos; this integration has created zero videos and modified zero historical snapshots or transcripts.

The external corpus is immutable. Configure its location at runtime; no code assumes a home directory or machine name:

```bash
export YIOS_WHAT_IF_CORPUS_ROOT="/path/to/video data of what if"
python scripts/validate_what_if_source_contract.py
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py
```

Run commands from repository root in a Python 3.12 environment with declared dependencies installed. First creation reports CREATED; the second run reports UNCHANGED. Promotion reports UNCHANGED when reproducing the already committed index.

## Data flow and durable local staging

The adapter validates the release manifest, source index, crosswalk and actual media hashes, then reads only eight canonical MASTER CSVs. It does not import legacy output or copy media. Normalization joins by exact approved YouTube identity, never by title. Unresolved and unregistered identities are held, not rejected or silently promoted.

Generated local staging lives at `data/staging/what-if-forensic/v1.0.0/` relative to repository root and is ignored by Git. Keep this directory in the durable checkout rather than a disposable worktree. It contains eight JSONL tables and deterministic `manifest.json`, which records release, transformation, source-manifest hash, catalog identity hash, accepted/held/rejected counts, table sizes and checksums. `lifecycle.json` separately records its UTC creation timestamp and deterministic manifest checksum. Keeping wall-clock metadata separate preserves byte-identical evidence reproduction. Existing creation time survives repeated generation. Old valid stages acquire lifecycle metadata only after their deterministic files validate.

Every normalized observation preserves canonical video ID, source video ID, slug, release, table, local row ID, CSV row number, timing, supplied confidence, media hash, original fields and transformation version. A source reference resolves as configured corpus root plus `production_intelligence_brain/01_master_data/<table>.csv#row=<n>`; the fragment identifies the CSV row and is not part of the filesystem path.

Current accepted/held/rejected rows:

| Table | Source | Accepted and promoted | Held | Rejected |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MASTER_WORDS | 7,864 | 5,817 | 2,047 | 0 |
| MASTER_SENTENCES | 604 | 485 | 119 | 0 |
| MASTER_SHOTS | 200 | 146 | 54 | 0 |
| MASTER_STATES | 581 | 352 | 229 | 0 |
| MASTER_MOTIONS | 438 | 289 | 149 | 0 |
| MASTER_ASSETS | 448 | 323 | 125 | 0 |
| MASTER_AUDIO_EVENTS | 29 | 21 | 8 | 0 |
| MASTER_AUDIO_VISUAL_SYNC | 1,421 | 894 | 527 | 0 |
| Total | 11,585 | 8,327 | 3,258 | 0 |

## Promotion and Editing/Visual consumption

Promotion reads the durable stage, revalidates every table checksum, counts, identity digest, observation key and provenance, then produces `data/intelligence/channels/CH-000004/forensic-observation-index-v1.json`. A different existing index fails with PROMOTION_CONFLICT; it is never replaced automatically. Promotion does not write to SQLite.

```bash
python scripts/query_what_if_forensics.py --video-id mEUqVgGf4e0 > /tmp/what-if-query.json
python scripts/run_youtube_intelligence.py \
  --channel CH-000004 --opportunity CH-000004-OP-001 \
  --generated-on 2026-10-09 --output-dir /tmp/what-if-production-plan
```

The compact query validates stage/index agreement before returning sampled shot pacing, state progression, motion actions/relationships, asset types and recurrence across unique videos, audio timing, narration/visual offsets, and the first 30 seconds of narration/edit pacing. Missing or non-finite timing never becomes a numeric measurement. Sampled shots do not establish complete-video coverage; changes per minute use sampled durations only. Recommendations remain EVIDENCE_BACKED_HYPOTHESIS, retain exact source rows and supplied confidence, and make no causal performance claim.

The orchestrator resolves opportunity video IDs through the canonical catalog and attaches matching guidance to the Editing/Visual blueprint. It preserves Topic, Packaging, Hook and Script artifacts. Four matching canonical videos contribute 2,381 observations and 24 cited hypotheses to the dated OP-001 example, without adding any channel samples. If local staging is absent, forensic consumption is explicitly NOT_AVAILABLE; if staging or index is changed, consumption fails closed. Historical editing reports remain preserved rather than rewritten.

## Review an update before promotion

Do not edit generated staging. Regenerate a candidate directory and candidate index, inspect the delta, and preserve current stage/index until review succeeds:

```bash
python scripts/stage_what_if_forensics.py --output /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate
python scripts/promote_what_if_forensics.py \
  --stage /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate --output /tmp/what-if-index-candidate.json
python -m json.tool data/staging/what-if-forensic/v1.0.0/manifest.json > /tmp/what-if-before.json
python -m json.tool /tmp/what-if-stage-candidate/manifest.json > /tmp/what-if-after.json
diff -u /tmp/what-if-before.json /tmp/what-if-after.json
git diff --no-index -- \
  data/intelligence/channels/CH-000004/forensic-observation-index-v1.json \
  /tmp/what-if-index-candidate.json
```

`diff` exits 1 for a legitimate difference. Review counts, mappings, media hashes, release and transformation changes. For a new source release, preserve the old corpus and contract; use a new versioned source contract and stage path with `--contract` and `--output`. After approval, archive the previous ignored stage outside the active path and replace it with the validated candidate. Update the reviewed index in an atomic PR and regenerate dated production outputs. Never change a recorded hash merely to suppress a mismatch.

A source table or identity change invalidates staging/promotion; regeneration is required. Source-declared evidence and AI recommendations stay separate. No forensic row is an independent channel sample.

## Identity refresh and unresolved sources

The owner explicitly authorized a narrow official YouTube Data API refresh for CH-000004 on 2026-10-09, superseding the no-API rule only for this task. Repository currently has controlled Apify acquisition, but no existing `channels.list`/uploads/`playlistItems.list` acquisition implementation; no YouTube/Google API credential was available in the execution environment. Apify acquisition requires a separate approved cost cap and was not run as a substitute.

There is currently no executable official refresh command to document honestly. Do not invoke a guessed script or register videos from search snippets. Once API authorization is available, the official acquisition must follow: `channels.list(part=contentDetails)` to identify the channel's uploads playlist; paginate `playlistItems.list(part=contentDetails)`; then `videos.list(part=snippet)` for exact channel ownership, title and publish time. Preserve sanitized response provenance and retrieval timestamp; register only genuine new IDs through the catalog registration workflow with append-only metadata snapshots. Review a 83-video baseline diff before publication. Credential values must remain environment-only.

SRC01 candidate U8F7UNK9jco has a matching sunset question on the official public video search result. SRC02 candidate qu8nx1qUwEU has matching visible-light question text. Their media metadata contains encoding/duration information but no authoritative video ID. Direct official page fetches were throttled. These are research candidates, not verified source-byte identity joins; crosswalk stays UNRESOLVED and promotion excludes both.

## Rollback

Catalog identities, snapshots and transcripts are not changed by stage/promotion/query work, so no data migration rollback is needed. Preserve the immutable external corpus and ignored stage.

For a published change, revert the specific integration merge in a new review branch, selecting the exact merge SHA from GitHub. Do not reset shared main or force-push:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git switch -c codex/what-if-rollback origin/main
git revert -m 1 <integration-merge-sha>
python -m pytest -q
git diff --check
```

Review dependent later commits before reverting; revert dependent units newest first. Submit the revert through normal PR/CI/exact-head merge. For local generated staging rollback, move the current ignored stage to a retained archive path and regenerate the previous reviewed contract at its deterministic path. Restore the matching reviewed promotion index via a PR. No raw media or historical evidence should be deleted.

## Privacy and raw-media policy

No raw MP4, audio, dense frames, Studio exports, credentials, temporary query outputs, or duplicated release packages may enter this What If integration. Keep source corpus and generated stages local. Commit only reviewed contracts, checksums, code/tests/docs and derived summaries with provenance. New private-derived analytics belong under ignored first-party storage.

Pre-existing tracked audio/frames/private-derived artifacts are separately classified in [repository safety review](audits/WHAT_IF_REPOSITORY_SAFETY_2026-10-09.md). They are not silently removed by this integration. Broader repository sharing or history rewriting requires an explicit owner/security decision.

- [Provenance lifecycle](PROVENANCE.md)
- [Data privacy](DATA_PRIVACY.md)

Continuation recovered source-declared collection dates for 595 existing records, adding 547 eligible performance comparisons without new acquisition. Script full reads increased to 17, semantic title records to 30. Five additional Drive triages yielded no independent finance data. [Performance/date evidence](PERFORMANCE_AND_VIRALITY.md), [Drive disposition](DRIVE_FOLLOWUP.md).

Original scripts can improve unit/comparator checks and label fictional scenarios. Audio confirmation remains outstanding. [Script analysis](SCRIPT_INTELLIGENCE.md).
- **Readable thumbnails are useful but insufficient.** Twenty-seven images were reviewed at mobile width; simple images occur in every tier. Current images are not verified historical packaging. [Thumbnail library](THUMBNAIL_PATTERN_LIBRARY.md).

Test household liquidity, borrowing-cost mechanics, total ownership/use cost and one historical leverage case. Each episode should answer one concrete question with an original worked example and a meaningful exception. Avoid another interchangeable quiet-millionaire story or unsupported market-doom prediction. # Script DNA — Casually Finance

Evidence base: 16 Whisper-base transcripts (10 long-form, 6 Shorts), 248 existing semantic beats (`03_MASTER_DATA/MASTER_SEMANTIC_BEATS.csv`), 206 descriptions (labelled `DESCRIPTION_PROXY`), and the dated performance tiers in `research/casually-finance-success-playbook/VIDEO_PERFORMANCE.csv` (branch `fb1e56d`). Coverage limits are in TRANSCRIPT_COVERAGE.md. Excerpts are kept short (≤12 words); everything else is paraphrased. No narration is reproduced.

Labels: `OBSERVED_PATTERN` (in the saved text), `PERFORMANCE_ASSOCIATION` (descriptive, same-format, age-adjusted, non-causal), `PLAUSIBLE_HYPOTHESIS`, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`.

---

## A. Opening hooks

### Shorts (all 6 transcripts)

| Video_ID (tier, ratio) | First-sentence type | Short excerpt (ASR) | Topic named by | Core mechanism starts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rSa2aziEsAI (BREAKOUT 11.85) | Paradox | "solved its debt problem by buying its own debt" | 0–3.3 s | 7.5 s |
| JsK53moCyZA (BREAKOUT 7.83) | Superlative + named person | "the largest initial public offering in human history" | 0–4 s | 4.4 s (scale), 21.5 s (who buys) |
| 6S3PzAUFnXQ (BREAKOUT 5.11) | Stacked-condition question | "why isn't this already a full-blown crisis?" | 0–6.5 s | 6.9 s |
| PxgCsLSf-w4 (too young to score) | Aphorism / definition | "long enough that no election survives it" | 0–9.6 s | 18.6 s |
| YGC3ao005as (too young to score) | Dated event | "On August 18, the 30-year touched…" | 0–4.3 s | 4.6 s |
| 2EZzwupIa80 (too young to score) | Absolute negation | "Nothing inside American politics forces anyone…" | 0–3.6 s | 3.9 s |

- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: every Short names its subject in the **first sentence** (ends between 3.3 and 9.6 s), and 5 of 6 begin the mechanism or evidence **by 7.5 s**. None opens with a greeting, a channel mention or a promise like "in this video".
- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: no single hook type dominates (6 different types across 6 Shorts). What they share is a **claim that contradicts a default expectation**: self-funded debt, a loss-making record IPO, a debt load with no crisis, a 30-year rate as "honest opinion", and so on.
- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: the financial stakes are national or systemic in 5 of 6. Only the SpaceX Short pivots to the viewer ("the answer is you").

### Long-form (10 transcripts)

| Period | Video_ID | Hook type | Time to central question |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | o3FQcd91MIs | Fictional persona ("Meet Dave") + comic escalation | ~64 s |
| 2025 | dlBhLhn8lL0 | Satirical list of money-burning fads | ~24 s (promise) |
| 2025 | kwMHrTFCWUE | Satirical setting + "nobody knows" punchline | ~17 s |
| 2026 | 5umJ63d3rzQ | Negation reframe ("was never the AI bubble") → hidden risk | ~18–31 s ("It starts in Tokyo") |
| 2026 | -X6YzlY_8tM | Superlative + comparison stack | ~21 s |
| 2026 | 0ll9rEtoRrs | "Biggest story for the past two weeks" + twist ("wasn't American") | ~11–15 s |
| 2026 | DgbHW0IqHrI | "A few days ago" dated auction + "at what cost?" | ~6 s |
| 2026 | xtqbRt94TTw | "Last week" Fed hike + vote-count paradox | ~27 s ("So what changed?") |
| 2026 | Uumnx2Fo6cE | "Last month" Redfin seller-surplus paradox | ~14 s |
| 2026 | roe3SgezmmU | "Chart going viral right now" + two-bar contrast | ~52 s |

- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: **tone shift**. All 3 transcribed 2025 long-forms open with comedy or persona. 6 of 7 transcribed 2026 long-forms open on a **dated, sourced data point or news event** ("a few days ago", "last week", "last month", "right now"). Temporal anchors occur 1.85 times per 1k words in 2026 long-forms and 0 times in 2025.
- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: the 2026 pattern is fact → contradiction → question within 6–31 s, then **elimination of easy explanations** before the real mechanism (housing B003, Fed B005–B007, IPO B003–B005).

## B. Storytelling structures (not one template)

### Six distinct Short structures

| ID | Structure | Example | Ending |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Paradox → mechanism chain → "armchair" objection → trap reveal → binary close | rSa2aziEsAI (61 s) | Complete answer, two-option tradeoff |
| S2 | Question → mechanism with 2 numbers → caveat → official projection → dated turning point → metaphor | 6S3PzAUFnXQ (69 s) | Complete answer + dated consequence |
| S3 | Superlative → comparison stack → rhetorical question → personal reveal → teaser | JsK53moCyZA (43 s) | **Open loop** (the rule is never explained) |
| S4 | Dated event → official response → quote → reaction → op-ed | YGC3ao005as (63 s) | Ends on a quoted line (abrupt) |
| S5 | Negation → parallel negations → authority credentials → quote → humour beat → aphorism → imperative | 2EZzwupIa80 (75 s) | Prescriptive one-liner |
| S6 | Aphorism → definition → escalation → "back up first" → dated evidence | PxgCsLSf-w4 (65 s) | **Open loop** (escalation, no answer) |

- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: **3 of 6 deliver a complete causal answer** (S1, S2, S5). **2 end on an open loop** (S3, S6) and 1 ends abruptly on a quote (S4). The open endings are a by-product of cutting a long-form mid-argument (§D), not necessarily a deliberate teaser strategy (`PLAUSIBLE_HYPOTHESIS`).
- `OBSERVED_PATTERN`: **one central mechanism per Short.** No Short introduces a second unrelated mechanism.

### Long-form grammar (2026, 7 transcripts)

Hook fact → contradiction / central question → eliminate easy answers → promise of a structural explanation (often numbered: "three things", "four separate things") → chapters of named-actor evidence → **sponsor at 22–55% of runtime** (5umJ63d3rzQ 55%, -X6YzlY_8tM 52–61%, 0ll9rEtoRrs 22–28%, DgbHW0IqHrI 41%, xtqbRt94TTw 45%, Uumnx2Fo6cE 47%, roe3SgezmmU 25%) → explicit return line ("Now back to…", 8 uses) → escalation → pre-emptive counterargument ("I know what some of you are thinking") → payoff/takeaway → CTA, which often comes **before** the final takeaway (85–97% of runtime). `OBSERVED_PATTERN`.

The 2025 long-forms have no sponsor beat and use enumerated comic archetypes (kwMHrTFCWUE) or a fictional-character arc (o3FQcd91MIs).

## C. Writing style (measured)

> The Fed raised rates in September to fight inflation. One of the first bills to go up was its own.
>
> Banks park about $3 trillion at the Fed, and it pays them interest at a rate that moves the moment the Fed moves. But the Fed earns mostly from bonds, many bought in 2020 and 2021, when 10-year yields averaged under 1.5%. Those don't reset.
